messages.subject: getting multinom to ignore irrelevant factor levels
messages.subject_clean: getting multinom to ignore irrelevant factor levels
messages.body_plain:
I am investigating diachronic change in Old French embedded verb-first (V1) clauses, and in particular, to what degree the type of subject attested (full nominal subject, subject pronoun, or pro) changes over time (c. 980-c.1280).

Dependent variable: subject-type (Stype: pro, Sn, Sp, tr)
Predictors: clause-type (cltype: cnjctl, advbl, nonSwh, Swh)
                 Date: dates of the texts used

I'm interested only in those types of embedded clauses that could have overt subjects, so I have subset my dataframe to exclude Swh (clauses in which the subject has been relativized or questioned). Once these are gone, there are a handful of Stype=tr that I also want to exclude, so I subset the dataframe to eliminate them as well. This leaves a dataframe that looks like this:

> summary(V1EMBCLSDATEINV, maxsum = 20)
      Date        Text         Vpos          SVorder       cltype           Stype        genre
 Min.   : 980     Alx : 47   V?:   0       na :1053      cnjctl:292      pro:1052   prose:437
 1st Qu.:1120   Auc : 17   V1:1408   SV :   0       advbl :558      S  : 339    verse:971
 Median :1180   BorP: 16   V2:   0    SXV:   0      nonSwh:558   Sp :  17
 Mean   :1178   BorV:191   V3:   0    VS : 297      Swh   :  0       tr :   0
 3rd Qu.:1220   Brn :208                   VXS:  58
 Max.   :1279   Cas : 40
                     Clr : 18
                      EusF: 40
                      EusM:  6
                      EusP:152
                     Leg : 17
                     MdF :100
                     PsT : 99
                    QLv :126
                    Qst : 17
                    Rol :118
                   SAg : 12
                   SR  : 96
                   Yvn : 88
> str(V1EMBCLSDATEINV)
'data.frame': 1408 obs. of  7 variables:
 $ Date   : int  980 980 980 980 980 980 980 980 980 980 ...
 $ Text   : Factor w/ 19 levels "Alx","Auc","BorP",..: 11 11 11 11 11 11 11 11 11 11 ...
 $ Vpos   : Factor w/ 4 levels "V?","V1","V2",..: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 ...
 $ SVorder: Factor w/ 5 levels "na","SV","SXV",..: 4 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 ...
 $ cltype : Factor w/ 4 levels "cnjctl","advbl",..: 2 1 1 2 1 1 3 3 3 3 ...
 $ Stype  : Factor w/ 4 levels "pro","S","Sp",..: 2 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 ...
 $ genre  : Factor w/ 2 levels "prose","verse": 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 …

I've worked my way through the explanation of multinomial regression with categorical and numerical predictors in the textbook StatForLing with R, and have done my best to develop my code in the same way, but the function multinom is paying attention to the removed and irrelevant factor levels tr and Swh--the latter turns up in the coefficients both as a main effect and an interaction, though the statistic given is of course 0. And I get warnings that "the group ‘tr’ is empty".

> V1.mlt <- multinom(Stype ~ cltype*Date, data=V1EMBCLSDATEINV)
# weights:  27 (16 variable)
initial  value 1546.846102
iter  10 value 790.425178
iter  20 value 780.612834
iter  30 value 777.245609
iter  40 value 777.157299
iter  50 value 776.828419
iter  60 value 776.209524
iter  70 value 776.104327
final  value 776.104184
converged
Warning message:
In multinom(Stype ~ cltype * Date, data = V1EMBCLSDATEINV) :
  group ‘tr’ is empty
> summary(V1.mlt, Wald=TRUE)
Call:
multinom(formula = Stype ~ cltype * Date, data = V1EMBCLSDATEINV)
Coefficients:
   (Intercept) cltypeadvbl cltypenonSwh cltypeSwh        Date cltypeadvbl:Date cltypenonSwh:Date cltypeSwh:Date
S    -11.70985  -0.0135306    -1.602733         0 0.007651655      0.001561583       0.002737894              0
Sp   -63.81664  30.3726778    44.004604         0 0.049132115     -0.025838716      -0.035544153              0

> anova(V1.mlt, multinom(Stype ~ cltype+Date))
# weights:  18 (10 variable)
initial  value 1546.846102
iter  10 value 834.227511
iter  20 value 780.917898
iter  30 value 780.172469
final  value 780.030782
converged
Likelihood ratio tests of Multinomial Models

Response: Stype
          Model Resid. df Resid. Dev   Test    Df LR stat.    Pr(Chi)
1 cltype + Date      2808   1560.062
2 cltype * Date      2804   1552.208 1 vs 2     4 7.853194 0.09710634
Warning message:
In multinom(Stype ~ cltype + Date) : group ‘tr’ is empty

> options(contrasts=c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
> Anova(V1.mlt, type="III")
Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III tests)

Response: Stype
            LR Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
cltype        7.8181  6     0.2517
Date         -0.2256  2     1.0000
cltype:Date   7.8532  6     0.2491
Warning messages:
1: In multinom(y ~ X[, term != asgn][, -1], weights = wt, trace = FALSE) :
  group ‘tr’ is empty
2: In multinom(y ~ X[, term != asgn][, -1], weights = wt, trace = FALSE) :
  group ‘tr’ is empty
3: In multinom(y ~ X[, term != asgn][, -1], weights = wt, trace = FALSE) :
  group ‘tr’ is empty

This can't help but interfere with getting the correct results, no? I've read all the help pages I can find on the web, and haven't found anything helpful. Has anyone else run into this?

Thanks!
